meta.title: After thirty years, a permanent home in Prague 6 — CB Dejvice
meta.description: CB Dejvice is building a sanctuary on Evropská Street in Prague 6. 54 million CZK project, 14 million already committed by members, 40 million still needed.
meta.governingPhrase: After thirty years, a permanent home in Prague 6

hero.headline: After thirty years, a permanent home in Prague 6
hero.subhead: For more than thirty years our congregation has worshipped in a rented hotel auditorium. We now have permission to build our own sanctuary — and 40,000,000 CZK (USD $1.89 million) left to raise.
hero.reassurance: Gifts are made by international bank transfer in CZK. Gifts made directly to CB Dejvice are not tax-deductible in the United States.

image.alt: The proposed sanctuary — a white perforated stone screen with a pointed-arch entrance — rendered into a photograph of the church building on Evropská Street today.

story.heading: A church without a room of its own
body: CB Dejvice was founded in 1995, just after the fall of communism, to bring the hope of the Gospel to Prague 6. Thirty years on, we are a congregation of about 150 members — large by Czech standards — in a district of 109,000 residents and 38,000 university students, many of whom have never set foot in a Protestant church. God has already used this church to plant another congregation in Prague.

In 2001 we bought a building on Evropská Street with a long-term hope: that one day it could hold everything we do. We have spent the years since renovating it. It is now full every day of the week with youth programmes, discipleship groups, counselling, community events and outreach. Every room is in use.

image.alt: The foyer of the church building, looking out toward Evropská Street past the café and the children’s-programme window.

beforeAfter.heading: Every Sunday, we leave
body: Then Sunday comes, and the entire congregation walks two kilometres up the road to a rented communist-era hotel auditorium. We have done this for more than thirty years. It is expensive, it takes a small army to set up and pack down each week, and it means the church our neighbours walk past all week is closed on the one morning they might think to come in.

In 2025, after more than twenty years of praying about it, we received permission to build a sanctuary on our own property. What once seemed impossible is now a set of drawings and a building permit in preparation.

before.alt: The church building on Evropská Street as it stands today.

after.alt: Architect’s render of the new entrance pavilion, with CÍRKEV BRATRSKÁ DEJVICE lettering on the wall.

cost.heading: Built underground
body: Prague 6's building regulations will not permit a conventional extension on this site. To build at all, the sanctuary has to go primarily below ground, excavated and constructed beneath the existing house. That is far more expensive than adding a hall on the side, and it is the single reason a 150-member church is looking at a 54-million-crown project.
We are not building something grand. We are paying what this city charges for a room to worship in.

image.alt: Section drawing showing the sanctuary hall built below ground, beneath the existing building.

money.heading: Where we stand
body: Our own members committed the first 14 million crowns, out of sacrificial giving, before we asked anyone outside the church for anything. The people closest to this project have already committed a quarter of it.
money.credibility: Application filed 29 June 2024. Valid zoning decision 17 July 2025. On 5 October 2025 our members voted, 100% of those present, to proceed. Full plans, floor plans and renderings are published at cb6.cz/modlitebna.

progress.ariaText: 14 million koruna committed of a 54 million koruna project — 26 percent

items.title: One roof
items.body: Worship, discipleship and outreach in the same building, instead of split across two addresses two kilometres apart.

items.title: An open door
items.body: A visible, welcoming public presence on the main road through Prague 6, so neighbours can see that a church is here and that they are welcome inside.

items.title: Room for who comes next
items.body: Space for families, for students, and for multiple Sunday services as new people explore faith.

items.title: An end to renting
items.body: Money that currently goes to a hotel every week goes into ministry instead.

image.alt: The finished sanctuary: pale oak seating, ribbed grey walls, and a slim cross lit by a skylight.

items.html: Gifts to the sanctuary project are made by international bank transfer to the church's dedicated sanctuary account at Raiffeisenbank. You will be charged in Czech crowns (CZK).
Use the payment reference exactly as shown above — it is what earmarks your gift for the sanctuary rather than for general church funds. Please do not replace it with your name.
If you would like your gift acknowledged, send your name and email to hospodar@cb6.cz after you transfer, and a person will answer you.
Questions about a gift, an acknowledgement, or a transfer from outside Europe: write to hospodar@cb6.cz.

Tax — please read before you give:
Gifts made directly to CB Dejvice are not tax-deductible in the United States. US law only allows a deduction for gifts to organisations formed in the United States, and CB Dejvice is a Czech church. There is no Gift Aid relief for UK donors either. We would rather tell you this plainly than have you find out afterwards. If deductibility matters to you, please write to hospodar@cb6.cz before you give and we will talk it through. Nothing here is tax advice — please consult your own adviser.

bank.title: The sanctuary account
bank.foot: Sending from outside Europe, or your bank asks for an IBAN or SWIFT code? Write to hospodar@cb6.cz and a person will send you what your bank needs.

items.q: Is my gift tax-deductible in the United States?
items.a: No. A US charitable deduction is only available for gifts to organisations formed in the United States, and CB Dejvice is a Czech church. A gift sent directly to us is not deductible on a US return, and UK donors cannot claim Gift Aid. If this matters to your giving, write to hospodar@cb6.cz before you send anything.

items.q: What currency am I charged in, and how does the money reach you?
items.a: Gifts arrive as an international bank transfer in Czech crowns (CZK) to the church's sanctuary account, carrying the payment reference shown in the giving section above. Your own bank sets the exchange rate and any transfer fee. Full account details are in the giving section.

items.q: Who receives the money, and what happens if the project changes?
items.a: Gifts go into the church's dedicated sanctuary account at Raiffeisenbank, held by CB Dejvice and designated for the sanctuary project by the payment reference. Project updates, drawings and permit progress are published at cb6.cz/modlitebna. Questions about how funds are handled go to hospodar@cb6.cz.

items.q: Can our church or foundation give as an institution?
items.a: Yes. Partner churches, foundations and institutional donors are welcome, and we are glad to answer diligence questions directly — hospodar@cb6.cz for the financial side, modlitebna@cb6.cz for the project.

items.q: Why is a sanctuary for 150 people so expensive?
items.a: Because Prague 6's regulations require it to be built primarily underground, beneath the existing building. Excavation and underground construction cost several times what a conventional hall would. See the section drawing above.

The hotel auditorium costs real money every week, sits two kilometres from the building where the rest of our life happens, and is invisible to the neighbourhood we are trying to reach. Building ends a recurring cost and puts the church where people can find it.

items.q: Can I see the actual plans?
items.a: Yes. Photographs, floor plans, section drawings and the full gallery of renderings are published at cb6.cz/modlitebna. Project questions go to modlitebna@cb6.cz.
